text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police invaded the lands and valuation ministry in search of evidence of an alleged house valuation scam involving top civil servants.
- Malawi has registered 1,198 refugees since asylum seekers from troubled Somalia, Rwanda, Burundi and Zaire began entering the country since 1994.

- Former president Kamuzu Banda said that his school, Kamuzu Academy, built at his home district of Kasungu in Central Malawi and widely known as the "Eton of Africa" is undergoing financial constraints after government pulled out annual subsistence.

- Surgical services at Lilongwe Central hospital on Thursday halted while the eye clinic at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, the country's biggest hospital, were closed following government decision to retire staff in the two departments.
- A German businessman may answer criminal charges after posing as a diplomat representing Cyprus interests in Malawi.
